components.note: 农 is the simplified form of 農, which depicted using a hoe 辰 to till a field 田 — an image of farming that gave rise to the meaning 'agriculture.'
巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.

example.hanzi: 这位农民种了三十年的水稻。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi nóngmín zhòngle sānshí nián de shuǐdào.
example.english: This farmer has grown rice for thirty years.
example.fact: Rice paddies flooded with water create an unusual ecosystem where farmers in parts of Asia raise fish or ducks alongside the crop — the animals eat pests and weeds while their waste fertilizes the soil, a practice called rice-fish co-culture that dates back over 1,700 years in China's Qingtian region, recognized today as a UNESCO-listed Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System.

components.note: 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which began as a pictograph of a scorpion, its body and pincers rendered in outline. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the number 'ten thousand,' a usage that eventually eclipsed the original meaning entirely.
Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'

example.hanzi: 这把万能钥匙能打开大楼里所有的门。
example.pinyin: zhè bǎ wànnéng yàoshi néng dǎkāi dàlóu lǐ suǒyǒu de mén.
example.english: This master key can open every door in the building.
example.fact: Locksmiths' "bump keys" exploit a real mechanical weakness in most pin-tumbler locks: a sharp rap on a specially cut key jolts the pins upward just long enough for the cylinder to turn, letting a single blank open thousands of different locks — a vulnerability documented since the 1970s and still a factor in modern lock design.

components.note: 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which began as a pictograph of a scorpion, its body and pincers rendered in outline. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the number 'ten thousand,' a usage that eventually eclipsed the original meaning entirely.
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息，她万分激动。
example.pinyin: tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā wànfēn jīdòng.
example.english: Hearing this news, she was extremely excited.
example.fact: The adrenaline surge behind intense excitement is produced by the adrenal medulla in under two seconds, triggering a heart-rate spike that can exceed 180 beats per minute — a response shaped by the same fight-or-flight pathway that let early humans react instantly to predators.

components.note: 口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.
纟 (silk/thread) — 红 originally described a color of dyed silk, hence 'red'
工 (gōng) gives a loose sound connection to 红's reading hóng

example.hanzi: 她出门前总要涂一点口红。
example.pinyin: tā chūmén qián zǒng yào tú yìdiǎn kǒuhóng.
example.english: She always puts on a little lipstick before going out.
example.fact: Lipstick is one of the oldest cosmetics on record: Sumerian women in ancient Mesopotamia crushed semi-precious gems into powder to redden their lips around 3500 BC, and Cleopatra later favored a red dye made from crushed carmine beetles and ants — a pigment chemically related to the carmine still used in some lipsticks today.

components.note: 办 (to manage/handle) — 协 relates to people working together to manage something
十 (shí) gives a sound distantly related to 协's reading xié, having drifted apart over time
讠 (speech) — relates to 调's meaning 'to adjust, transfer,' something coordinated through spoken negotiation.
周 (zhōu) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from diào.

example.hanzi: 教练负责协调球队的训练计划。
example.pinyin: jiàoliàn fùzé xiétiáo qiúduì de xùnliàn jìhuà.
example.english: The coach is responsible for coordinating the team's training schedule.
example.fact: The human cerebellum, which makes up only about 10% of brain volume, contains roughly 80% of the brain's neurons and is the primary structure responsible for coordinating fine muscle movement — damage to it produces a distinctive unsteady gait known as cerebellar ataxia.

components.note: 白 — a shining crown
王 (king) — the ruler wearing the crown
帝 depicts an altar stand used for sacrificial offerings to the gods — the one who presides over such rites came to be known as 帝, 'supreme ruler, emperor.'

example.hanzi: 秦始皇是中国历史上第一位皇帝。
example.pinyin: Qín Shǐhuáng shì Zhōngguó lìshǐ shàng dì yī wèi huángdì.
example.english: Qin Shi Huang was the first emperor in Chinese history.
example.fact: When Qin Shi Huang died in 210 BC, he was buried with an army of over 8,000 life-size terracotta soldiers, each with individually sculpted facial features, discovered by farmers digging a well in 1974 near Xi'an — one of the largest archaeological finds of the 20th century.

components.note: 敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
正 (zhèng) gives a sound hint — 整 is pronounced zhěng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
夕 (evening/night) — the darkness that has fallen
亻 (a person) — someone moving under cover of night

example.hanzi: 他整夜都没有睡着。
example.pinyin: tā zhěngyè dōu méiyǒu shuìzháo.
example.english: He didn't fall asleep the whole night.
example.fact: A single night of total sleep deprivation measurably impairs reaction time and judgment to a degree comparable with a blood alcohol content around 0.05%, according to sleep researchers — one reason many countries now treat drowsy driving as seriously as drunk driving in road-safety campaigns.

components.note: 比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'

艹 (grass) sits atop 萨's traditional form 薩, tying it loosely to plant life. The character was later repurposed mainly as a phonetic symbol used to transliterate foreign sounds, as in 菩萨 (bodhisattva) and 拉萨 (Lhasa).

example.hanzi: 我们周末想订一份比萨。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zhōumò xiǎng dìng yí fèn bǐsà.
example.english: We want to order a pizza this weekend.
example.fact: The Margherita pizza, topped with tomato, mozzarella, and basil to mirror the colors of the Italian flag, was reportedly created in Naples in 1889 in honor of Queen Margherita of Savoy — a founding story still printed on pizzerias' walls throughout the city today.

components.note: 亼 — traditionally linked to an image of gathering or covering; its original pictorial sense has become obscure, but the character came to mean 'now, the present.'
夕 (evening/night) — the darkness that has fallen
亻 (a person) — someone moving under cover of night

example.hanzi: 今夜的月亮特别圆。
example.pinyin: jīnyè de yuèliàng tèbié yuán.
example.english: Tonight's moon is especially round.
example.fact: A full moon looks measurably larger and brighter near the horizon than high overhead — an illusion called the "moon illusion" that has puzzled scientists for centuries, since photographs prove the moon's actual angular size stays constant no matter where it sits in the sky.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
网 (a net) sits above — in the traditional form 買, this pictures gathering something valuable.
贝 (a cowrie shell, used as ancient currency) — a net closing over shells of value gave 买 its meaning 'to purchase.'

example.hanzi: 有人试图收买这位法官。
example.pinyin: yǒurén shìtú shōumǎi zhè wèi fǎguān.
example.english: Someone tried to bribe this judge.
example.fact: Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index, first published in 1995, ranks over 180 countries each year by perceived public-sector corruption; consistently top-ranked nations like Denmark and New Zealand share features such as strong freedom-of-information laws and independent judiciaries that make bribery harder to conceal.

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 下雨了，他们决定不外出了。
example.pinyin: xiàyǔ le, tāmen juédìng bù wàichū le.
example.english: It's raining, so they decided not to go out.
example.fact: Storm clouds that produce heavy rain, called cumulonimbus clouds, can tower more than 12 kilometers into the atmosphere and contain enough water to fill hundreds of thousands of swimming pools — their rapid updrafts of over 160 km/h also generate the electrical charge separation behind lightning.

components.note: 岂 in 凯's traditional form 凱 pictures a ceremonial drum played to celebrate victory.
几 (a stand or table) sits beside it, together giving 凯 its meaning 'triumphant, victorious,' as in a homecoming celebration.
扌 (hand) — 撒 describes scattering something by hand.
散 (to scatter, to disperse) — combined with the hand 扌, it gave 撒 its meaning 'to scatter, to release.'

example.hanzi: 凯撒是古罗马著名的将军和政治家。
example.pinyin: Kǎisā shì gǔ Luómǎ zhùmíng de jiāngjūn hé zhèngzhìjiā.
example.english: Caesar was a famous general and statesman of ancient Rome.
example.fact: Julius Caesar's assassination on the Ides of March, 44 BC, was carried out by roughly 60 senators who reportedly stabbed him 23 times, yet a later Roman physician determined that only one wound — a chest stab — was actually fatal, with the rest inflicted after he had already collapsed.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 代 relates to a person's place in time.
弋 (a stake used to mark or catch something) — combined with 亻 (person), 代 came to mean a 'generation' or 'era,' and 'to take the place of' someone.
口 (mouth) — 号 relates to calling or crying out aloud, as well as a spoken or marked sign
丂 gives a loose sound connection to 号's reading hào

example.hanzi: 这次行动的代号是"曙光"。
example.pinyin: zhè cì xíngdòng de dàihào shì "shǔguāng".
example.english: This operation's code name is "Dawn."
example.fact: The 1944 Normandy invasion carried the code name "Operation Overlord," and to protect it Allied intelligence ran an elaborate deception campaign called Operation Fortitude — complete with inflatable tanks and fake radio traffic — that convinced German commanders the real attack would come at Calais, not Normandy.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 镇 originally referred to a heavy metal weight used to press something down, later extending to 'garrison town.'
真 (zhēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 镇's reading zhèn, differing only in tone.
青 (blue-green, nature) — 静 relates to a calm stillness, like still water or clear skies
争 (zhēng) gives a sound distantly related to 静's reading jìng, having drifted apart over time
刂 (knife) relates 剂 to cutting or dividing something into a prepared dose.
齐 (qí) has drifted apart from jì over time, sharing little of the original sound match.

example.hanzi: 医生给病人开了一些镇静剂。
example.pinyin: yīshēng gěi bìngrén kāile yìxiē zhènjìngjì.
example.english: The doctor prescribed some tranquilizers for the patient.
example.fact: Diazepam, sold under the brand name Valium, became the best-selling prescription drug in the United States for much of the 1970s, at one point accounting for over 2 billion pills sold annually — a scale of use that later prompted tighter regulation of benzodiazepine tranquilizers worldwide.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.

example.hanzi: 她是一名大三的大学生。
example.pinyin: tā shì yì míng dà sān de dàxuéshēng.
example.english: She is a third-year university student.
example.fact: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is generally recognized as the oldest continuously operating university in the world — its original students helped write the "Constitutio Habita" in 1158, a charter that granted traveling scholars legal protection, a founding document of academic freedom still cited today.

components.note: 天 (sky, standing in for the ruler above) suggests something reported upward to the emperor, the root of 奏's old meaning 'to present a memorial.'
攵 (an action/to strike) — 效 relates to the result produced by an action
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 效's reading xiào

example.hanzi: 新的治疗方法很快就奏效了。
example.pinyin: xīn de zhìliáo fāngfǎ hěn kuài jiù zòuxiào le.
example.english: The new treatment method quickly proved effective.
example.fact: Penicillin, discovered accidentally by Alexander Fleming in 1928 when a stray mold contaminated a petri dish, wasn't mass-produced as an effective treatment until the early 1940s — wartime demand during World War II drove production from a few doses to over 646 billion units per year by 1945.

components.note: 厃 depicts a steep, overhanging cliff edge.
㔾 depicts a person crouching — together with 厃, the image of someone perched at a cliff's edge gave 危 its meaning 'dangerous.'
宀 (a roof, house) sets the scene inside a home.
口 (mouth) — harsh words spoken within the house gave 害 its meaning 'to harm, injure.'

example.hanzi: 空气污染会危害人们的健康。
example.pinyin: kōngqì wūrǎn huì wēihài rénmen de jiànkāng.
example.english: Air pollution can harm people's health.
example.fact: The World Health Organization estimates that ambient and household air pollution together contribute to around 7 million premature deaths per year worldwide, making it one of the leading environmental health risks — fine particulate matter smaller than 2.5 micrometers is small enough to pass directly into the bloodstream through the lungs.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 缘 originally described the hemmed edge of cloth, extended to mean 'connection, fate.'
彖 (tuàn) gives a sound distantly related to yuán, having drifted apart over time.
攵 (an action) — ties to 故's sense of a cause or reason behind an action
古 (gǔ) gives a sound close to 故's reading gù

example.hanzi: 因为天气的缘故，比赛推迟了。
example.pinyin: yīnwèi tiānqì de yuángù, bǐsài tuīchí le.
example.english: Because of the weather, the match was postponed.
example.fact: The strangest weather-related sports disruption on record may be the 1975 English test cricket match abandoned not for rain but for a sudden, unseasonal snowfall in June — groundskeepers had to shovel a covering of snow off the pitch before play could even be considered.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 跟 originally referred to the heel of the foot, extended to mean 'to follow (on someone's heels)'
艮 (gèn) gives a loose sound connection to 跟's reading gēn
阝 (a mound/city) — represents a place being traveled to.
迶 depicts walking or moving along a path — following someone to the city gave 随 its meaning 'to follow, along with.'

example.hanzi: 小狗一直跟随着主人。
example.pinyin: xiǎo gǒu yìzhí gēnsuízhe zhǔrén.
example.english: The little dog kept following its owner.
example.fact: Dogs' ability to track and follow a specific person's scent trail relies on roughly 300 million scent receptors in their nose, compared to about 6 million in humans, and a brain region for processing smell that is proportionally many times larger than ours.

components.note: 大 (great, big) — boasting or praising both involve making something out to be great.
亏 (kuī) gives a sound close to kuā, sharing the initial consonant.
大 (big) — 奖 describes something given as a big reward.
丬 (qiáng) gives a sound close to jiǎng.

example.hanzi: 老师在课堂上夸奖了这个学生。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī zài kètáng shàng kuājiǎng le zhège xuésheng.
example.english: The teacher praised this student in class.
example.fact: A well-known 1998 study by psychologist Carol Dweck found that praising children for being "smart" after a task made them perform worse on subsequent challenges than praising their effort or strategy — a finding that reshaped classroom feedback practices around what researchers now call a "growth mindset."

components.note: 士 (a scholar/gentleman) — represents a person of learning and ambition.
心 (heart/mind) — the mind and aspirations of a scholar gave 志 its meaning 'purpose, will, ambition.'
心 (heart) — 愿 relates to a heartfelt wish or desire
原 (yuán) gives a loose sound connection to 愿's reading yuàn

者 originally depicted a plant with leaves branching above a mouth-like base; its early meaning is uncertain, but the character was borrowed to form a grammatical particle marking 'the one who...' or 'the thing that...,' as in 志愿者 'volunteer.'

example.hanzi: 地震发生后，许多志愿者前去救援。
example.pinyin: dìzhèn fāshēng hòu, xǔduō zhìyuànzhě qián qù jiùyuán.
example.english: After the earthquake, many volunteers went to help with the rescue.
example.fact: The 2010 Haiti earthquake relief effort drew tens of thousands of aid workers, and it also marked one of the first large-scale uses of crowdsourced crisis mapping — the open-source platform Ushahidi let volunteers worldwide plot real-time reports of trapped survivors onto a shared map within hours of the disaster.

components.note: 龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.
糸 (thread) — plain, undyed silk thread
龶 — a plant stem, from which the raw silk thread hangs

example.hanzi: 肝脏能帮助身体排出毒素。
example.pinyin: gānzàng néng bāngzhù shēntǐ páichū dúsù.
example.english: The liver helps the body eliminate toxins.
example.fact: Botulinum toxin, produced by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum, is often cited as the most acutely lethal substance known — yet in minute, carefully controlled doses it's the same toxin used medically as Botox to treat muscle spasms and wrinkles.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 铅 names a metal, lead.
几 (jī) gives a sound distantly related to qiān, having drifted apart over time.
⺮ (bamboo) depicts the shaft of a writing brush.
毛 (hair) depicts the bristled tip of the brush — together giving 笔 its meaning 'writing brush, pen.'

example.hanzi: 请用铅笔在这张纸上写字。
example.pinyin: qǐng yòng qiānbǐ zài zhè zhāng zhǐ shàng xiězì.
example.english: Please write on this paper with a pencil.
example.fact: Despite the name, pencils have never contained lead; the "lead" is actually a mixture of graphite and clay, a naming holdover from when graphite was first mistaken for a form of lead ore after a large deposit was discovered in Cumbria, England, in the 1500s.

components.note: 人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
合 pictures a lid 亼 fitted down over a container's mouth 口 — the image of two parts closing together neatly gave 合 its meaning 'to combine, to fit, to close.'

example.hanzi: 我们约好在车站会合。
example.pinyin: wǒmen yuē hǎo zài chēzhàn huìhé.
example.english: We agreed to meet up at the train station.
example.fact: The Apollo 11 mission's most technically delicate moment wasn't the moon landing but the subsequent orbital rendezvous, when the ascent stage carrying Armstrong and Aldrin had to precisely dock with the command module orbiting overhead — a maneuver with no margin for error, since there was no way to rescue the astronauts if it failed.

components.note: 讠 (speech) on the left shows this involves words.
秀 (elegant, refined) on the right suggests alluring words, giving 诱 its meaning 'to entice, to lure.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 橱窗里的蛋糕看起来非常诱人。
example.pinyin: chúchuāng lǐ de dàngāo kànqǐlái fēicháng yòurén.
example.english: The cake in the display window looks very tempting.
example.fact: The Venus flytrap lures insects with a sweet, nectar-like scent, but only snaps shut after two separate touch-sensitive trigger hairs are activated within about 20 seconds of each other — a built-in filter that keeps the plant from wasting energy closing on raindrops or debris.

components.note: ⺳ (a net) suggests something meant to catch things.
干 (dry, empty) sits inside it — an empty fishing net, giving 罕 its meaning 'rare, scarce.'
冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'

example.hanzi: 这种鸟在野外非常罕见。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng niǎo zài yěwài fēicháng hǎnjiàn.
example.english: This kind of bird is very rare in the wild.
example.fact: The kakapo, a flightless nocturnal parrot native to New Zealand, is one of the rarest birds on Earth: its total population dropped to just 51 individuals in 1995 before an intensive conservation program brought numbers back above 250 by the early 2020s, with every surviving bird individually named and radio-tagged.

components.note: 犭 (dog, beast) — 狩 (to hunt) was traditionally associated with hunting dogs.
守 (shǒu) gives a sound close to shòu, sharing the same sound and differing only in tone.
犭 (dog) shows 猎 relates to hunting with animals.
昔 (xī) gives a sound distantly related to liè, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 古代人靠狩猎和采集获取食物。
example.pinyin: gǔdài rén kào shòuliè hé cǎijí huòqǔ shíwù.
example.english: Ancient people obtained food through hunting and gathering.
example.fact: Analysis of ancient tools and animal bones suggests early humans were persistence hunters, chasing prey like antelope for hours across open savanna in the midday heat until the animal overheated and collapsed — a strategy made possible by humans' unusually efficient sweating and relatively hairless skin compared with other mammals.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.
廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'

example.hanzi: 他慢慢拉开了窗帘。
example.pinyin: tā mànmàn lākāi le chuānglián.
example.english: He slowly pulled open the curtains.
example.fact: Modern blackout curtains can block over 99% of incoming light by combining a tightly woven outer fabric with a rubberized or foam backing layer — a design originally developed for wartime blackout regulations in the 1940s to prevent city lights from guiding enemy bombers at night.

components.note: 尤 (particularly/outstanding) — relates to 就's sense of approaching or arriving at a particular point
京 (jīng, capital) gives a sound close to 就's pronunciation jiù
匕 here relates to a person crouching or sitting — 此 originally pictured 'this place' where someone is.
止 (zhǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 此 is pronounced cǐ, sharing a similar final though the initial has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 双方就此达成了协议。
example.pinyin: shuāngfāng jiùcǐ dáchéng le xiéyì.
example.english: The two sides reached an agreement from that point on.
example.fact: The Camp David Accords, signed in 1978 after 13 days of secluded negotiation between Egypt and Israel brokered by U.S. President Jimmy Carter, marked the point from which Egypt became the first Arab nation to formally recognize Israel — a peace treaty that has held for more than four decades since.

meanings: (fig.) first place in a women's competition

components.note: 后 merges two historically separate characters. As 後 ('after, behind'), it pictured a foot 夂 trailing behind on a path, tied together with a thread 幺 — the image of lagging steps.

As 后 ('queen, ruler'), it separately pictured a person facing backward while issuing a command from a position of authority. The two unrelated characters were merged into one simplified form, 后, which today can mean both 'after' and 'empress/queen.'
广 (a wide, open building) — a hall or pavilion
坐 (to sit) — a seat placed inside the building

example.hanzi: 孩子们坐在汽车的后座上。
example.pinyin: háizimen zuò zài qìchē de hòuzuò shàng.
example.english: The children are sitting in the back seat of the car.
example.fact: Rear-seat seatbelt laws lagged far behind front-seat requirements in most countries — the United States didn't see a major federal push for rear-seat belt use until the 1980s — even though crash studies show unbelted rear passengers can strike front-seat occupants with enough force to injure or kill them too.

components.note: 水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

example.hanzi: 鱼在水中自由地游来游去。
example.pinyin: yú zài shuǐzhōng zìyóu de yóu lái yóu qù.
example.english: Fish swim freely back and forth in the water.
example.fact: Water is roughly 800 times denser than air, which is why aquatic animals like whales can grow far larger than any land animal — buoyancy supports their weight so their skeletons don't need to bear the same load a similarly sized land creature's would.

meanings: see 安寧區|安宁区[An1 ning2 Qu1]
see 安寧市|安宁市[An1 ning2 Shi4]

components.note: 宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
宀 (roof) — a peaceful home under a roof relates to 宁's meaning 'calm, serene.'
丁 (dīng) gives a sound distantly related to níng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 乡村的生活十分安宁。
example.pinyin: xiāngcūn de shēnghuó shífēn ānníng.
example.english: Life in the countryside is very peaceful.
example.fact: Finland topped the UN's World Happiness Report for multiple consecutive years running up to the 2020s, and researchers studying the ranking point to factors like extensive access to nature, low income inequality, and high social trust — Finland has one of the highest ratios of forest and lake area per capita in Europe.

components.note: 为 is the simplified form of 爲, which pictured a hand 爪 grasping the trunk of an elephant 象 — perhaps depicting the guiding or domestication of the animal for work, an image that gave rise to the meaning 'to do, to act as, to make.'
又 (a hand) — reaching out to try to catch something.
隹 (a bird) — catching a bird by hand is hard, giving 难 its meaning 'difficult.'

example.hanzi: 他的问题让老师有点为难。
example.pinyin: tā de wèntí ràng lǎoshī yǒudiǎn wéinán.
example.english: His question put the teacher in a bit of a difficult spot.
example.fact: The "trolley problem," a thought experiment first posed by philosopher Philippa Foot in 1967, deliberately puts people in an impossible moral bind — divert a runaway trolley to kill one person or let it kill five — and has since become a standard tool for studying real-world ethical dilemmas in fields from medicine to self-driving car design.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恶 relates to an evil or malicious state of heart/mind
亚 (yà) gives a sound distantly related to 恶's reading è, having drifted apart over time
少 (few, little) — suggests something lacking or insufficient, the root idea behind 'inferior.'
力 (lì) gives a sound that's a close but not exact match for liè — they share the initial and a similar rhyme.

example.hanzi: 由于天气恶劣，航班被取消了。
example.pinyin: yóuyú tiānqì èliè, hángbān bèi qǔxiāo le.
example.english: Due to the bad weather, the flight was cancelled.
example.fact: Mount Washington in New Hampshire once recorded a wind gust of 372 km/h in 1934, long considered the fastest surface wind speed ever measured directly by an anemometer — its notoriously severe weather results from storm tracks from the Gulf of Mexico, the Atlantic, and the Pacific all converging over the same small peak.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 炸 relates to a sudden burst of fire, an explosion.
乍 depicts something happening abruptly — combined with fire, giving 炸 its meaning 'to explode, to deep-fry.'
扌 (hand) — 掉 relates to dropping something from the hand.
卓 (zhuó) reflects an older phonetic connection that has faded in the modern pronunciation diào.

example.hanzi: 工程队把那座旧桥炸掉了。
example.pinyin: gōngchéngduì bǎ nà zuò jiù qiáo zhàdiào le.
example.english: The engineering crew blew up that old bridge.
example.fact: Controlled demolition engineers use a technique called "implosion," precisely timing hundreds of small explosive charges to detonate in sequence so a building collapses straight down into its own footprint — the technique lets crews safely demolish structures on cramped city blocks without damaging neighboring buildings.

components.note: 升 originally pictured a ladle or measuring dipper used to scoop grain, related to the character 斗. Because such measures were held up and tipped, the character came to mean both a unit of volume and, by extension, 'to rise, to ascend.'
走 (to walk/run) — 起 relates to standing up and setting into motion.
己 (jǐ) gives a close sound cue — 起 is pronounced qǐ, sharing the same final sound.

example.hanzi: 太阳慢慢从东方升起。
example.pinyin: tàiyáng mànmàn cóng dōngfāng shēngqǐ.
example.english: The sun slowly rises from the east.
example.fact: Because Earth's rotation axis is tilted about 23.4 degrees, the exact point on the horizon where the sun rises shifts throughout the year, reaching its northernmost point at the June solstice and its southernmost at the December solstice — ancient structures like Stonehenge were deliberately aligned to track these seasonal extremes.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 铁 refers to iron, a metal
失 (shī) gives a sound distantly related to 铁's reading tiě, having drifted apart over time
足 (foot) — relates to 路's meaning 'road, path,' something walked on with feet.
各 (gè) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lù.

example.hanzi: 这条铁路连接了两座城市。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo tiělù liánjiē le liǎng zuò chéngshì.
example.english: This railroad connects two cities.
example.fact: The First Transcontinental Railroad, completed in the United States in 1869 at Promontory Summit, Utah, cut coast-to-coast travel time from roughly six months by wagon to about a week by train — its construction relied heavily on thousands of Chinese immigrant workers, particularly on the treacherous Sierra Nevada crossing.

meanings: in the twinkling of an eye

components.note: 目 (eye) shows the open eye.
乏 here stands in for the other eye, closed — together depicting the quick blink of the eyes.
目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 她一眨眼就不见了。
example.pinyin: tā yì zhǎyǎn jiù bùjiàn le.
example.english: In the blink of an eye, she was gone.
example.fact: Humans blink an average of 15 to 20 times per minute — far more often than needed just to keep the eyes lubricated — and researchers have found that a large share of blinks happen at natural pause points during reading or conversation, suggesting the brain uses blinking as a brief, ultra-short mental reset.

meanings: (said of an aging husband) my old man

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 那个老头子每天早上都去公园散步。
example.pinyin: nàge lǎotóuzi měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán sànbù.
example.english: That old man goes for a walk in the park every morning.
example.fact: Jeanne Calment of France holds the verified record for the longest confirmed human lifespan, dying in 1997 at 122 years and 164 days old — she reportedly took up fencing at 85 and continued riding a bicycle until age 100, and her longevity record has stood unbroken for over two decades.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
钅 (metal) marks the material — hooks are typically made of metal.
勾 (a hook shape) sits beside it — a curved metal tool, giving 钩 its meaning 'hook.'

example.hanzi: 那条鱼终于上钩了。
example.pinyin: nà tiáo yú zhōngyú shàng gōu le.
example.english: That fish finally took the bait.
example.fact: Anglerfish use a bioluminescent lure grown from a modified fin spine that dangles above their mouths, and the light comes not from the fish itself but from colonies of symbiotic bacteria living inside the lure — a partnership that lets the fish attract prey in total darkness thousands of meters below the surface.

components.note: Hand — putting pieces together by hand.
Gives the sound bìng, related to pīn but drifted apart over time.
图 is the simplified form of 圖, which pictured a district's borders 啚 enclosed within a boundary 囗 — an old image of a map, giving 图 its meaning 'picture, chart, map.'

example.hanzi: 我们花了三个小时才拼好这幅拼图。
example.pinyin: wǒmen huāle sān gè xiǎoshí cái pīn hǎo zhè fú pīntú.
example.english: It took us three hours to finish this jigsaw puzzle.
example.fact: The jigsaw puzzle was invented around 1760 by London mapmaker John Spilsbury, who mounted a map on wood and cut along country borders to create an educational toy for teaching children geography — the "jigsaw" name only came later, once mechanical jigsaws made cutting interlocking pieces practical for mass production.

components.note: 丷 depicts two small horns.
兄 here forms the body of a creature — together an early image of a horned animal; the character later shifted to mean 'to exchange, convert.'
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — a valuable object one might glimpse or notice.
见 (to see) — catching sight of something links to the meanings 'to appear, present, now.'

example.hanzi: 他终于兑现了自己的承诺。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú duìxiàn le zìjǐ de chéngnuò.
example.english: He finally honored his promise.
example.fact: The world's oldest known written promissory contracts come from ancient Mesopotamia around 2000 BC, inscribed in cuneiform on clay tablets that recorded loans of silver or grain to be repaid by a specified date — an early legal framework for turning a spoken promise into an enforceable, cashable obligation.

components.note: 走 (to walk/run) — 起 relates to standing up and setting into motion.
己 (jǐ) gives a close sound cue — 起 is pronounced qǐ, sharing the same final sound.
衤 (clothing) — the cloth that is about to be cut
刀 (a knife) — cutting the cloth is the first step in making clothes

example.hanzi: 起初他并不相信这个消息。
example.pinyin: qǐchū tā bìng bù xiāngxìn zhège xiāoxi.
example.english: At first, he didn't believe the news at all.
example.fact: Alfred Wegener's 1912 theory of continental drift was met with near-universal rejection by geologists, who found the idea that continents slowly moved across Earth's surface implausible without a mechanism to explain it — it wasn't until the 1960s discovery of seafloor spreading that his originally dismissed idea became mainstream geology.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刺 describes the action of piercing or stabbing with something sharp.
朿 (cì) gives the sound — an exact match with 刺's reading cì.
乂 depicts crossed strokes suggesting a cutting action.
木 (wood) here represents a wooden stake — giving 杀 its meaning 'to kill.'

example.hanzi: 历史上有很多国王死于刺杀。
example.pinyin: lìshǐ shàng yǒu hěn duō guówáng sǐ yú cìshā.
example.english: Throughout history, many kings have died from assassination.
example.fact: Franz Ferdinand's assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, succeeded only after an earlier bomb attack that day had failed — his driver then took a wrong turn directly past the same group of conspirators, giving Gavrilo Princip a second, unplanned chance that set off the chain of events leading to World War I.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 停 relates to a person coming to a halt
亭 (tíng) gives the sound — an exact match with 停's reading tíng
田 (a field) sits at the base, anchoring the character to a fixed place.
The element above depicts something being kept or set aside rather than taken away — together with the field below, 留 came to mean 'to stay, to remain, to keep.'

example.hanzi: 我们在香港停留了两天。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài Xiānggǎng tíngliú le liǎng tiān.
example.english: We stayed in Hong Kong for two days.
example.fact: Hong Kong's old Kai Tak Airport was famous among aviation enthusiasts for its approach directly over the rooftops of Kowloon's dense apartment blocks, with pilots making a sharp last-second turn at low altitude before landing — a maneuver retired when the airport moved to its current Chek Lap Kok location in 1998.

components.note: 石 (rock) — 碰 originally described one hard object, like a stone, striking another, giving 'to bump, to collide.'
並 (bìng) is only distantly related in sound to pèng — both use a bilabial initial (b/p), but the rhyme and tone have drifted apart.
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 我们下午三点在图书馆碰面。
example.pinyin: wǒmen xiàwǔ sān diǎn zài túshūguǎn pèngmiàn.
example.english: We're meeting at the library at 3pm.
example.fact: The Library of Alexandria, founded in Egypt around the 3rd century BC, is estimated to have held several hundred thousand papyrus scrolls at its peak and attracted scholars from across the ancient Mediterranean — its gradual decline and eventual loss remains one of history's most cited symbols of how much recorded knowledge can vanish.

meanings: (of the people in a group) to get into position (idiom)

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to walk) — 各 pictures people arriving from different directions.
口 (mouth) — different people speaking gave 各 its meaning 'each' or 'every,' emphasizing individual distinctness.
尤 (particularly/outstanding) — relates to 就's sense of approaching or arriving at a particular point
京 (jīng, capital) gives a sound close to 就's pronunciation jiù
夂 (a foot, to walk) — 各 pictures people arriving from different directions.
口 (mouth) — different people speaking gave 各 its meaning 'each' or 'every,' emphasizing individual distinctness.
亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.

example.hanzi: 裁判喊道："各就各位，预备，跑！"
example.pinyin: cáipàn hǎndào: "gè jiù gè wèi, yùbèi, pǎo!"
example.english: The referee shouted, "On your marks, get set, go!"
example.fact: Modern Olympic starting blocks are equipped with force sensors that detect a runner's push-off within one-thousandth of a second — since 2010, any sprinter who reacts in under 0.1 seconds after the starting gun is automatically disqualified, since that's faster than the fastest possible human reaction time.

components.note: 黑 (black/dark) pictures nightfall.
犬 (dog) pictures a dog keeping silent watch in the dark, giving 默 its meaning 'silent, still.'
Now stands in for what was originally a piece of wood.
Represents notches cut into the wood to mark an agreement.

example.hanzi: 老搭档之间总有一种默契。
example.pinyin: lǎo dādàng zhījiān zǒng yǒu yì zhǒng mòqì.
example.english: There's always a kind of unspoken understanding between old partners.
example.fact: Studies of elite doubles tennis and volleyball teams have found that long-term partners develop measurably faster nonverbal coordination — reacting to a teammate's body position in as little as 200 milliseconds — a learned synchrony researchers attribute to thousands of hours of shared practice rather than any special innate ability.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 追 relates to moving in pursuit of someone or something
㠯 (yǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 追's reading zhuī, having drifted apart over time
辶 (to walk) — 逐 means to chase or pursue, involving movement.
豕 (shǐ) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading zhú has diverged.

example.hanzi: 猎豹在草原上追逐着猎物。
example.pinyin: liè bào zài cǎoyuán shàng zhuīzhú zhe lièwù.
example.english: The cheetah chases its prey across the grassland.
example.fact: Cheetahs can accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in about 3 seconds — faster than most sports cars — but their sprints rarely last longer than 30 seconds, since the heat generated by their muscles at top speed would otherwise push their body temperature to dangerous levels.

components.note: 阝 (a hill/place) — 陆 relates to solid ground, as opposed to water
击 (jī) gives a sound distantly related to 陆's reading lù, having drifted apart considerably over time
冖 here is a distorted form of 力 (strength) — a simplified way of showing soldiers grouped together.
车 (cart/vehicle) — 军 originally pictured soldiers riding out to battle in war chariots.

example.hanzi: 他退伍前是陆军上尉。
example.pinyin: tā tuìwǔ qián shì lùjūn shàngwèi.
example.english: Before he retired from the military, he was an army captain.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army buried near Xi'an represents one of history's most detailed records of ancient ground forces: its roughly 8,000 soldiers include distinct infantry, archers, and charioteers arranged in actual military formation, giving archaeologists a rare, precise blueprint of how China's earliest imperial army was organized.
